events.title: In the Room: Sixty Years on the Front Lines of History
events.description: Roosevelt understood the camera before most politicians did. He posed in buckskin in the Badlands, stood with John Muir at Yosemite, and left behind one of the most photographed lives of his century. David Hume Kennerly has spent sixty years doing the other half of that job — from the Vietnam battlefields that earned him the Pulitzer, to the Ford White House, to nearly every administration since. The special exhibition, drawn from his book In the Room, opens at the Library in October.

events.title: The Panama Canal: Power, Politics, and Ambition
events.description: Historian Ralph Nurnberger argues why the Panama Canal can be seen as either a landmark achievement of American diplomacy or a symbol of U.S. arrogance and corruption. Closely tied to Theodore Roosevelt’s vision of global power, the canal became both a strategic success and a long-running controversy. Nurnberger traces its history, including the debate over transferring control to Panama, while examining why the United States built a canal in another country and why Panama was selected.

venue.address: This online program is presented on Zoom.

events.title: Elkhorn Evenings
events.description: On two Thursdays in December, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library stays open after hours. At the Branding Market, participants choose a wood or leather item and watch it branded on the spot, or try the branding iron themselves. Items range from small keepsakes to larger gifts. At the Salt+Scoria counter, participants can build their own charcuterie board from local goods and take it home or enjoy it there. The exhibits stay open throughout the evening.

events.title: Theodore Roosevelt Association Strenuous Life Adventure Africa Expedition
events.description: Africa Expedition | June 4–14, 2027 Retrace one of the greatest adventures in American history. From June 4–14, 2027 , join the Theodore Roosevelt Association on an extraordinary journey through Kenya, following the route of President Theodore Roosevelt's legendary 1909–1910 Smithsonian–Roosevelt African Expedition. Guided by Don Young , CEO of Newland, Tarlton & Co. —the same safari company that outfitted Theodore Roosevelt's original expedition—this exclusive experience blends history, wildlife, luxury, and adventure into the u ltimate "Strenuous Life" experience.
